content.json:
# Diagnostic Settings Inspector

Read-only v1: find resources in a selected scope, then inspect **one exact resource ID**. Uses Azure Resource Graph (ARG) for inventory and live Azure Resource Manager (ARM) metadata for diagnostic settings and supported categories. No logs, keys, configuration changes, or backend.

## 1. Selected-scope inventory
Choose subscriptions and resource groups. This is the inventory visible to your account, **not a confirmed production estate**. The filters below apply only to inventory, not to the independent inspector in section 2.

parameters.name: Subscriptions
parameters.label: Inventory subscriptions
parameters.description: Select explicit subscriptions. Keep the scope small; the ARG source supports at most 1,000 subscriptions per query.

parameters.name: ResourceGroups
parameters.label: Inventory resource groups
parameters.query:
ResourceContainers
| where type =~ 'microsoft.resources/subscriptions/resourcegroups'
| project value = tolower(id), label = strcat(name, ' | ', subscriptionId), selected = false
| order by label asc
parameters.description: Values are full resource group IDs; identical names in different subscriptions stay distinct. All means all resource groups in the selected subscriptions. Recheck this selection after changing subscriptions.

content.query:
Resources
| extend ResourceGroupId = tolower(strcat('/subscriptions/', subscriptionId, '/resourceGroups/', resourceGroup))
| where '*' in ({ResourceGroups}) or ResourceGroupId in~ ({ResourceGroups})
| summarize Resources = count()
content.title: Selected-scope resource count (ARG; not diagnostic coverage)

content.json: ARG is RBAC-filtered and eventually consistent. The count is a server-side aggregation for the selected scope; the list below intentionally shows **at most 1,000 resources**, not a complete export. If the count exceeds 1,000, narrow the scope. Dropdowns also have a 1,000-item limit; use fewer subscriptions if resource groups are missing. Grid search only searches returned rows and does not change the count. Count and list refresh independently.

content.query:
Resources
| extend ResourceGroupId = tolower(strcat('/subscriptions/', subscriptionId, '/resourceGroups/', resourceGroup))
| where '*' in ({ResourceGroups}) or ResourceGroupId in~ ({ResourceGroups})
| project Name = name, Type = type, ResourceGroup = resourceGroup, SubscriptionId = subscriptionId, Location = location, ResourceId = id
| order by ResourceId asc
| take 1000
content.title: Selected-scope inventory - copy a ResourceId for section 2 (up to 1,000)
content.noDataMessage: No resources returned for the selected inventory scope.

content.json:
## 2. Independent single-resource inspector

Copy one full **ResourceId** from the inventory (click its cell for details) or from the resource's **Properties / JSON View** in Azure, then paste it below. Use the ID, not a portal URL; no trailing slash, query string, fragment, or URL encoding.

**Inventory subscriptions and resource groups do not constrain or change this target.** It may be outside that scope. Changing inventory filters deliberately leaves this target unchanged; clear or replace it explicitly. Check the exact target displayed below before interpreting results.

For service children not listed by ARG, paste the exact child ID. For example, for an existing storage account's Blob service, append `/blobServices/default` to its account ID. v1 does not discover children or combine parent and child settings. A parent storage account and its Blob service are different targets.

parameters.name: TargetResourceId
parameters.label: Exact resource ID to inspect (independent of inventory)

paramValidationRules.message: Paste one full resource-group-scoped ARM resource ID, including provider/type/name pairs. Do not use a URL, whitespace, encoded characters, query string, fragment, or trailing slash.

parameters.description: Required before ARM queries run. Supports direct service-child IDs. Subscription, resource-group, tenant, and management-group targets are outside v1.

content.json:
**Exact ARM target (independent of inventory):**

`{TargetResourceId}`

The following are two separate live reads, not an atomic snapshot. Use the workbook **Refresh** control to reread metadata. A 403, 404, 429, or other request failure is an error, **not** an empty result, unsupported resource, or compliance decision.

content.title: Live diagnostic settings - all returned settings, with their entries and destinations

content.json:
**Reading settings:** one row is one diagnostic setting. Click **LogEntries** or **MetricEntries** to expand every JSON entry; `enabled: true` and `enabled: false` are preserved, as are `category` and `categoryGroup`. Click **Setting** for row details including the full destination identifiers, or scroll the grid horizontally. Entries belong only to the destinations on the same row. An absent optional array/field means the API did not supply it; it is not proof that the resource is unsupported. `logAnalyticsDestinationType` is the API value (for example, `Dedicated`), not an inferred mode.

An empty-success message applies only to its own completed request. Do not interpret results while either panel is loading or showing an error.

content.title: Live supported categories and group memberships - exact target only

content.json:
## How to compare and what v1 cannot tell you

Compare each setting's log `category` with the live **Category** names. For a `categoryGroup`, inspect **CategoryGroups** membership (click to expand). Compare metric entries only with **Metrics** categories. **Available does not mean recommended**; v1 does not recommend `allLogs` or evaluate a baseline.

Metric export is different from resource logs and from metrics available in Metrics Explorer; not every metric or dimension is exportable through diagnostic settings. Configuration metadata does not prove data is arriving at a destination. This workbook does not read log contents, destination contents, or keys.

This is a current, one-resource inspector: **no estate-wide configured/missing totals, production classification, compliance scoring, recommendations, history, or remediation**. ARM `GETARRAY` follows collection pages; it does not query every inventory resource. Both ARM tables have a 10,000-row display ceiling; a display limit is not a completeness guarantee. Different resource types, child services, RBAC, API availability, throttling, and refresh timing can affect results. v1 accepts resource-group-scoped IDs only and does not discover service children.

Viewers need access to the underlying resources as well as the workbook; sharing a workbook grants neither. Saving the workbook is the user's separate Azure action and requires workbook write permission in an approved resource group. No Azure tenant was accessed during development; local checks do not substitute for a portal smoke test.

[README, import steps, permissions, and limitations](https://github.com/ppmiralles0110/DiagnosticSettingsMonWS/blob/ppmiralles0110-diagnostic-workbook-v1/README.md) | [Diagnostic settings documentation](https://learn.microsoft.com/en-us/azure/azure-monitor/essentials/diagnostic-settings)
